status: fermion matching and phenomenology audit of the claim-1607 healthy 0-minus torsion EFT patch

conventions.torsionVector: S^mu=epsilon^{alpha beta gamma mu}T_{alpha beta gamma}
conventions.minimalDiracBenchmark: c_f=1/8 in this S_mu convention, up to an overall sign that drops out of identical-species exchange

exactExchangeKernel.interpretation: the transverse axial torsion is algebraic and gives a local axial-axial operator; only the longitudinal divergence carries the 0-minus pole

canonicalPseudoscalarMatching.derivativeCouplings: L_int=sum_f f_f partial_mu varphi J_5,f^mu with f_f=c_f/sqrt(a_S)
canonicalPseudoscalarMatching.wardIdentity: partial_mu J_5,f^mu=2 i m_f bar(psi_f)gamma_5 psi_f + gauge-anomaly terms
canonicalPseudoscalarMatching.onShellYukawa: L_int=-i sum_f y_f varphi bar(psi_f)gamma_5 psi_f plus anomaly terms, with y_f=2m_f f_f
canonicalPseudoscalarMatching.e6Qualification: the E6-to-Spin(10)-to-SM representation chain supplies chiral fermion slots but does not fix c_f, the exotic thresholds, flavor rotations, or anomaly coefficients; minimal geometry gives a universal elementary-fermion benchmark, not an E6-specific numerical prediction

lowEnergyMatching.dimensionSixWilsonMatrixConvention: with L_eff=-(1/2)sum_fg C_AA,fg J_5,f.J_5,g, C_AA,fg=c_f c_g/a_S
lowEnergyMatching.dimensionEightLongitudinalMatrix: with +(1/2)sum_fg C_dA,fg (partial.J_5,f)(partial.J_5,g), C_dA,fg=c_f c_g b_X/a_S^2=c_f c_g/(a_S m_phi^2)
lowEnergyMatching.minimalEinsteinCartanMagnitude: for c_f=1/8 and lambda=0, the single-current coefficient c^2/(2a_S)=3/(16 M_Pl^2), matching the conventional Einstein-Cartan four-fermion magnitude up to signature/sign conventions

staticPolePotential.operatorForm: V_pole(r)=+f_1 f_2 sigma_1^i sigma_2^j partial_i partial_j Y_m(r) in the Fadeev-et-al. corrected-sign convention
staticPolePotential.separateLocalTerm: the algebraic -J_c^2/(2a_S) operator adds a zero-range spin-spin interaction; it is not part of the separated-body Yukawa tail
staticPolePotential.selection: unpolarized macroscopic sources average the one-pseudoscalar dipole-dipole force to zero; polarized torsion balances, comagnetometers, atomic spectroscopy and spin-precession experiments are the direct probes

finiteWitness.interpretation: order-one b_X and a noncritical torsion mass coefficient put the pole at the Planck scale and all fermion effects at gravitational strength

decouplingAndCriticalLimits.result: m_phi to infinity and the propagating Yukawa tail disappears, while the algebraic Einstein-Cartan axial-axial contact remains

decouplingAndCriticalLimits.limit: a_S to infinity at fixed c_f and b_X
decouplingAndCriticalLimits.result: both f_f and the contact Wilson coefficient vanish
the fermion portal vanishes even though the pure torsion pole remains
m_phi decreases and f_f diverges at fixed b_X; this is not a controlled enhancement because the Dirac constraint matrix loses rank at a_S=0
the separated-body pole potential is exponentially suppressed, leaving only unresolved contact physics

observableMap.laboratorySeparatedSpinSources: the potential is precisely the generic pseudoscalar dipole-dipole potential tested by torsion pendula, trapped spins, magnetometers and comagnetometers; Terrano et al. cover mediator masses up to 500 micro-eV and report sensitivities to couplings up to 14 orders below electromagnetism
observableMap.atomicAndMolecular: the delta-function and short-range tensor pieces shift hyperfine/spin-dependent levels; nuclear and electronic matrix elements are required before applying spectroscopy limits
observableMap.colliderAndContact: for m_phi above momentum transfer the observable is an axial-axial contact operator; ordinary propagating axial-vector torsion resonance bounds do not map directly because this sector has no transverse pole
observableMap.stellarElectrons: as a historical light-pseudoscalar benchmark, Raffelt and Weiss give alpha_a<0.5e-26, equivalent to y_e<sqrt(4 pi alpha_a) about 2.5e-13; stellar-systematic reassessments make this a benchmark rather than a universal hard wall
observableMap.supernovaNucleons: Lella et al. find that combined supernova arguments exclude roughly g_aN greater than 1e-9 for masses below about 1 MeV, subject to trapping and supernova-model assumptions
observableMap.minimalBenchmarkComparison: at delta=1 the minimal values y_e=2.57e-22 and y_N=4.72e-19 are respectively about nine and ten orders below those representative astrophysical sensitivities
observableMap.nearCriticalTranslation: for the minimal benchmark y_f(delta)=y_f(delta=1)/sqrt(delta), so the historical electron bound corresponds to delta=1-4lambda greater than about 1.1e-18 and the supernova nucleon benchmark to delta greater than about 2.2e-19, only when their mass ranges and coupling assumptions apply
observableMap.hadronicCaveat: the nucleon coefficient is a spin-fraction matching combination of quark c_q, not automatically the elementary universal c_f

rangeNaturalness.decision: a laboratory/stellar-range pole with the minimal weak coupling requires an enormous b_X; using only critical tuning with order-one b_X makes f_f diverge, crosses observational benchmarks first, and approaches the constraint-rank boundary

fermionLoopClosure.powerCounting: two insertions of c_f S_mu J_5,f^mu in a Dirac loop have superficial degree two and generate local dimension-four torsion operators
fermionLoopClosure.nonzeroSpurion: for any charged c_f, beta_{F_S^2} at F_S^2=0 is nonzero; the ultraviolet transverse axial-current polarization is the same nonvanishing tensor structure as vector vacuum polarization, up to mass/anomaly terms
fermionLoopClosure.generatedOperator: F_S,mu nu F_S^{mu nu}, where F_S,mu nu=partial_mu S_nu-partial_nu S_mu, together with mass-dependent longitudinal/local terms
fermionLoopClosure.consequence: the fermion-coupled Xhat^2-only surface is not radiatively closed; a transverse spin-1 torsion pole is activated after resummation and the full spin-parity ghost/tachyon test must be repeated
fermionLoopClosure.scope: as an EFT the generated term is perturbative below the cutoff; it is nevertheless fatal to claiming an exact one-mode fundamental portal

decision.classification: generic torsion/axion-like EFT portal, not yet a distinctive Spin(2,3) prediction
decision.reason: the force shape is the standard pseudoscalar dipole-dipole potential and the mass and coupling depend on free b_X, lambda and c_f; the E6 descendant has not fixed flavor or anomaly coefficients
decision.potentialFingerprint: a distinctive portal would require the UV construction to fix c_f ratios, b_X and lambda, producing the correlated relation f_f m_phi=c_f/sqrt(b_X), plus anomaly coefficients and exotic-threshold matching
decision.minimalExpectation: with natural order-one b_X and away from lambda=1/4 the mediator is Planck-mass and decoupled; observable long range requires a huge b_X or a near-degenerate a_S, both demanding additional protection

stopRules: Do not apply transverse axial-vector resonance bounds to a purely longitudinal 0-minus pole.
Do not call the coupling E6-universal until the descendant action fixes c_f, flavor rotations and exotic thresholds.
Do not use lambda=1/4 as a massless limit: the canonical constraint rank changes there.
Do not apply stellar or supernova bounds outside their mediator-mass, free-streaming/trapping and production assumptions.
Do not claim a monopole-dipole force without an independently generated scalar CP-violating coupling; the minimal portal is dipole-dipole.
Require a radiative mechanism protecting any huge b_X or tiny 1-4lambda used to put the mode in laboratory range.
Once c_f is nonzero, include the fermion-loop-generated transverse torsion operators before claiming a fundamental one-pole spectrum.
